# Injury Risk: Injured, Recovering and Chronic Cases

**Summary.** Only the true chronic cases should cost less: players with repeated problems in the same lower-body spot, like Kawhi Leonard's knee, Joel Embiid's knees, Stephen Curry's runner's knee or Coby White's calf, and Kristaps Porzingis with his mystery illness. Treat one-off injuries and Achilles or ACL returns as normal bids with a dip in minutes early in the season, and do not stack several injury risks on one roster. Our 4 IL slots only take players listed Out, so use them for 1 USD final-pick stashes such as Jimmy Butler, not for players tagged Q.

## Chronic cases: price them down

The main rule: be careful with players who have repeated injuries or surgeries to the same lower-body part, especially knees, or an ongoing mystery illness. Repeated problems in the same spot make more missed time likely. Draft these players below their per-game value. At our auction, that means you stop at the expert cap. Do not pay their per-game value or what our league paid last season. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=873), [06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=547))

The clearest chronic cases in our pool: Kawhi Leonard has a degenerative knee with repeated meniscus, ACL and tendon problems in the same knee. Joel Embiid has repeated knee problems and surgeries and may play only 40 to 50 games. Stephen Curry has runner's knee and calls it a new normal, so plan for 15 to 30 missed games. Coby White has had four calf strains in 12 months. Zach Edey has had repeated foot and ankle surgeries. Kristaps Porzingis has an ongoing mystery illness plus knee and ankle problems. ([Kawhi Leonard](../profiles/players/kawhi-leonard.md), [Joel Embiid](../profiles/players/joel-embiid.md), [Stephen Curry](../profiles/players/stephen-curry.md), [Coby White](../profiles/players/coby-white.md), [Zach Edey](../profiles/players/zach-edey.md), [Kristaps Porziņģis](../profiles/players/kristaps-porzingis.md))

A healthy season does not erase a degenerative injury. Keep the chronic discount even if the player stayed healthy last year. For a player like Leonard, check every week for new knee news and count how many back-to-backs he plays. ([06-30](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=380), [Kawhi Leonard](../profiles/players/kawhi-leonard.md))

Some injuries do not justify a discount. Hand, finger, shoulder and oblique injuries matter little, and concussions matter only a little. Walker Kessler's shoulder surgery and finger tag, Collin Murray-Boyles's thumb and Kyshawn George's arm injury should not lower your bid. Anthony Davis falls in between. He has had many different injuries, mostly lower body, but no single recurring one. Experts doubt only his games played and set the bar at about 60, so buy him only at a discount. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=873), [Walker Kessler](../profiles/players/walker-kessler.md), [Collin Murray-Boyles](../profiles/players/collin-murray-boyles.md), [Kyshawn George](../profiles/players/kyshawn-george.md), [Anthony Davis](../profiles/players/anthony-davis.md))

## Coming back from injury: one-off, not chronic

Returning players have a hidden cost. They usually play under minutes limits and miss back-to-backs while they ramp up, so all of their numbers drop. Tyrese Haliburton is expected to have early limits from Carlisle, with back-to-backs monitored. Damian Lillard is expected to play about 30 to 31 minutes. Fred VanVleet should start near 30 and rise to about 34. Brandon Ingram is expected to have a minutes limit when he returns. ([10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1700), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=386), [Tyrese Haliburton](../profiles/players/tyrese-haliburton.md), [Damian Lillard](../profiles/players/damian-lillard.md), [Fred VanVleet](../profiles/players/fred-vanvleet.md), [Brandon Ingram](../profiles/players/brandon-ingram.md))

Do not overreact, though. Drafters are too scared of players returning from an injury that cost them last season, and the season is 25 weeks long. Jayson Tatum's Achilles, Franz Wagner's high ankle sprain, Trae Young's 15-game season and Anthony Edwards's 61 games are one-off events without a chronic tag. Bid on them in their normal expert range. Kon Knueppel's hamstring, which gets re-evaluated in week one, and James Harden's ankle are short-term problems. ## Load management and back-to-backs

Back-to-back counts matter mostly for injury-prone players, so the schedule hurts the chronic cases most. The Raptors have three back-to-backs in our playoff weeks, and Leonard is expected to sit some. The Sixers also have three in our playoff weeks, and Embiid sits all of them. Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league, which matters for Donovan Mitchell's knees and Evan Mobley's calves. Curry and Porzingis play on a Warriors team with 15 back-to-backs, and Irving plays on a Dallas team with 16. Luka Doncic's calf and hamstring face the Lakers' heavy back-to-back schedule. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/sf6Ga9k-r-Q?t=1686), [Kawhi Leonard](../profiles/players/kawhi-leonard.md), [Joel Embiid](../profiles/players/joel-embiid.md), [Donovan Mitchell](../profiles/players/donovan-mitchell.md), [Evan Mobley](../profiles/players/evan-mobley.md), [Stephen Curry](../profiles/players/stephen-curry.md), [Kristaps Porziņģis](../profiles/players/kristaps-porzingis.md), [Kyrie Irving](../profiles/players/kyrie-irving.md), [Luka Dončić](../profiles/players/luka-doncic.md))

Planned rest without a chronic injury is a smaller problem. The Knicks plan to be careful with starters for about the first 30 games: Karl-Anthony Towns, Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby, Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges. Carlisle rests players on back-to-backs, which affects Pascal Siakam and Ivica Zubac. LeBron James projects to about 65 games, and Victor Wembanyama's minutes are managed so that he does not reach 35 a night. Expect lower totals early in the season. Check minutes in the first weeks, and do not treat these players as injury risks. ([Karl-Anthony Towns](../profiles/players/karl-anthony-towns.md), [Jalen Brunson](../profiles/players/jalen-brunson.md), [OG Anunoby](../profiles/players/og-anunoby.md), [Josh Hart](../profiles/players/josh-hart.md), [Mikal Bridges](../profiles/players/mikal-bridges.md), [Pascal Siakam](../profiles/players/pascal-siakam.md), [Ivica Zubac](../profiles/players/ivica-zubac.md), [LeBron James](../profiles/players/lebron-james.md), [Victor Wembanyama](../profiles/players/victor-wembanyama.md))

## Using our 4 IL slots

Yahoo removed IL+. Players tagged Out or injured can go on IL right away, but questionable, doubtful and probable players cannot. Haliburton, Irving, Coby White, Dereck Lively and Porzingis are all Q right now. Until they are downgraded to Out, they take up a bench or active spot. Do not plan your roster as if they will sit in an IL slot. ([09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=292), [Tyrese Haliburton](../profiles/players/tyrese-haliburton.md), [Kyrie Irving](../profiles/players/kyrie-irving.md), [Coby White](../profiles/players/coby-white.md), [Dereck Lively II](../profiles/players/dereck-lively.md), [Kristaps Porziņģis](../profiles/players/kristaps-porzingis.md))

Do not draft or stash a long-term injured player as a core piece. Keep him only in an empty IL slot, and drop him once you need the spot. Jimmy Butler (out with a torn ACL, back around Christmas or January) and Yanic Konan Niederhauser (broken foot, back around Christmas) are 1 USD final picks only. Ingram (partially torn Achilles, back around Thanksgiving to Christmas) is a 1 to 3 USD late stash at most. ([09-14](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=2182), [Jimmy Butler III](../profiles/players/jimmy-butler.md), [Yanic Konan Niederhäuser](../profiles/players/yanic-konan-niederhauser.md), [Brandon Ingram](../profiles/players/brandon-ingram.md))

Skip players who will be back too late to help. Mark Williams returns in mid to late March at best, so he is not worth a dollar or an IL slot. Shaedon Sharpe, Ariel Hukporti, Henri Veesaar and Richie Saunders are expected to miss our whole season. Players like Moses Moody and Donte DiVincenzo, who may return around March, belong on a waiver watch list, not on draft day. ## Do not stack risks

Do not load up on several players with injury worries. Before every bid on a chronic-tier player, count the big risks already on your roster. For example, if you already own Leonard, pass on Embiid or Curry and spend on a player with no injury tag. IL slots cannot hold players who are resting, so a roster of load-managed stars leaves empty days. In head-to-head that means empty weeks, especially in our playoffs. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1769), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=1343), [Kawhi Leonard](../profiles/players/kawhi-leonard.md), [Joel Embiid](../profiles/players/joel-embiid.md), [Stephen Curry](../profiles/players/stephen-curry.md))

## Where the experts disagree

Ingram: one expert says he is fine around picks 100 to 110 in formats that allow stashing. The newest view is to skip him inside the top 120. With our 4 IL slots and a 4-3-4 Clippers playoff schedule, that only supports a 1 to 3 USD late stash. ([Brandon Ingram](../profiles/players/brandon-ingram.md))

Jalen Green had three hamstring strains last season, which looks like a chronic same-spot case. But one expert says it is not a concern now. Markkanen played 42 games, and experts are split on how many of his recent absences were real injuries and how many were tank holdouts. ([Jalen Green](../profiles/players/jalen-green.md), [Lauri Markkanen](../profiles/players/lauri-markkanen.md))

Kevin Durant: the Rockets say they will cut his minutes, but Lloyd doubts it and expects 35 to 36. At about 33 minutes, Lloyd says his value changes materially. Check his minutes in the first weeks. ([Kevin Durant](../profiles/players/kevin-durant.md))

On the method itself, one note says to avoid players who start the season injured. Another says drafters are too scared of players returning from last season's injuries. Both can apply in our league. Fade players who are Out on draft day, but bid with confidence on players who are healthy now after an injury last season. ([09-27](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=561), [09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=1258))
